sections.title: Chemical Reactions — Change with New Substances
sections.content: Reaction = reactants → products via rearranged atoms (bonds break/make, nuclei unchanged). Physical change = state/colour only (water→steam, no new substance); Chemical change = new substances with new properties (CuSO4+Fe → FeSO4+Cu). Observations: gas evolution, temperature change, precipitate, colour, state. At given T & concentration, rate predictable; heat often speeds via activation energy.

sections.title: Word Equations & Symbols
sections.content: Word equation: Sodium + Chlorine → Sodium chloride (plus separates multiple reactants/products). Symbol: element code (Na, Cl), valency = combining capacity (electrons lost/gained/shared). Chemical equation uses symbols/formulae with states: (s),(l),(g),(aq), ↑ gas, ↓ precipitate.

sections.title: Balancing — Law of Conservation of Mass
sections.content: No atoms created/destroyed; mass reactants = mass products. Balanced equation has equal atoms each side. Use coefficients (numbers in front). Example Zn + 2HCl → ZnCl2 + H2. Hit-and-trial: change coefficients until atoms equal. Shortcut: algebraic simultaneous equations (aCaCO3+bH3PO4→cCa3(PO4)2+dH2CO3 → a=3c, a=d, 3a+4b=8c+3d, 3b=2d, b=2c → c=1→a=3,b=2,d=3).
sections.visual: Scale: left atoms = right atoms, coefficient slider

sections.title: Types — Combination to Redox
sections.content: Combination: CaO+H2O→Ca(OH)2 (exothermic, heat). Decomposition: HgO→Hg+O2 (heat), H2O2→H2O+O2 (light), H2O→H2+O2 (electric). Displacement: Fe+CuSO4→FeSO4+Cu (more reactive displaces). Double displacement: AgNO3+KCl→AgCl↓+KNO3 (precipitate). Redox: oxidation (lose e⁻, gain O, lose H) + reduction (gain e⁻) simultaneous, e.g., CuO+H2→Cu+H2O. Exothermic (Al+Fe2O3→Al2O3+Fe+heat) vs Endothermic (6CO2+6H2O+Sun→C6H12O6+6O2). Corrosion: 4Fe+3O2+xH2O→2Fe2O3·xH2O (rust), Cu green, Ag black. Rancidity: fats oxidize → foul smell, prevented by air-tight, N2, refrigeration, antioxidants.

solvedExamples.solution: Set aCaCO3+bH3PO4→cCa3(PO4)2+dH2CO3 → Ca: a=3c, C: a=d, O:3a+4b=8c+3d, H:3b=2d, P:b=2c → c=1→a=3,b=2,d=3 → 3CaCO3+2H3PO4→Ca3(PO4)2+3H2CO3. Visual: atom count table.

solvedExamples.q: Why does AgCl turn black in sunlight?
solvedExamples.solution: Photolytic decomposition: 2AgCl→2Ag+Cl2, light breaks Ag-Cl, Ag darkens. Same as H2O2 photolysis.

sections.title: What is Acid/Base/Salt
sections.content: Acid: sour, turns blue litmus red, H+ donor (Arrhenius: H+ / H3O+, Bronsted: H+ donor, e.g., HCl). Base: bitter, turns red litmus blue, H+ acceptor, OH- donor (NaOH, KOH). Salt: neutral, anion of acid + cation of base (KCl, NaNO3), from neutralization. Household: acids in curd/lemon, bases in soap/toothpaste.
sections.visual: Litmus strips: blue→red (acid), red→blue (base), purple neutral; methyl orange, phenolphthalein

sections.title: Reactions — With Metals, Carbonates, and Each Other
sections.content: Acid+metal → salt+H2+heat (2HCl+Mg→MgCl2+H2), base+metal→salt+H2 (2NaOH+Zn→Na2ZnO2+H2). Acid+carbonate/bicarbonate → salt+water+CO2 (2HCl+CaCO3→CaCl2+H2O+CO2, effervescence, lime water milky). Metal oxide/hydroxide (basic) + acid → salt+water (H2SO4+MgO→MgSO4+H2O). Non-metal oxide (acidic) + base → salt+water (2NaOH+CO2→Na2CO3+H2O). Strong acid+strong base → NaCl+H2O (HCl+NaOH).
sections.visual: Three beakers: metal fizz, carbonate fizz with lime water, neutralization to salt+water

sections.title: Water — Dilution & Strength
sections.content: Acids/bases dissociate in water → conduct electricity. Base vs alkali: all alkalis are bases (OH- in water, e.g., NaOH), not all bases are alkalis (insoluble like CuO). Hydronium H3O+ forms. Dilution is exothermic — add acid to water, not reverse. Strong = fully dissociates (HCl, NaOH), weak = partially (CH3COOH), dilute vs concentrated = ions per volume.
sections.visual: Dilution: acid into water (safe) vs water into acid (spatter), strong/weak dissociation bars

sections.title: pH — The 0-14 Scale
sections.content: pH=-log10[H+], pure water [H+]=[OH-]=10^-7 → pH 7. <7 acidic, >7 basic. Universal indicator 0-14. Importance: plants/animals need pH 6.5-7 (soil), digestion 1.5-4 (HCl), tooth decay <5.5, bee/nettele defence acid.
sections.visual: pH chart 0-14 with lemon 2, water 7, soap 10, blood 7.4, garden pH meter

sections.title: Salts — From Common Salt
sections.content: Salt = anion+cation. Family by same ion (NaCl,KCl). pH: strong acid+strong base → neutral 7, weak acid+strong base → basic >7, strong+weak → acidic <7. From NaCl: NaOH via chlor-alkali (electrolysis brine → Cl2 at anode, H2 at cathode, NaOH remains), Bleaching powder Ca(OCl)Cl via Ca(OH)2+Cl2 → CaOCl2+H2O (bleach, oxidizer, disinfectant), Baking soda NaHCO3 via Solvay CaCO3→CaO+CO2 then NaCl+NH3+CO2+H2O→NaHCO3+NH4Cl (antacid), Washing soda Na2CO3, Plaster of Paris CaSO4·½H2O via gypsum CaSO4·2H2O heated at 100°C → CaSO4·½H2O+3/2H2O (cast). Crystals have water of crystallisation.
sections.visual: Salt family tree: NaCl → 4 branches (NaOH, Bleaching, Baking, Washing, POP) with process arrows

sections.title: Reproduction — Why & How
sections.content: Multiply to increase population, continue species. Unicellular & multicellular (bacteria, algae, plants, animals, humans) via fission, budding, fragmentation, spore, vegetative, sexual.
sections.visual: Tree of life: fission (Paramecium), budding (yeast), spore (fungi), vegetative (bryophyllum)

sections.title: Asexual — Fission, Budding, Fragmentation, Spore, Vegetative
sections.content: Fission: binary (Paramecium 2) vs multiple (Plasmodium many). Budding: yeast/hydra small cyst, may stay attached. Regeneration (lizard) vs fragmentation (Planaria/Hydra pieces → whole). Spore: fungi sporangia, thick wall, germinate when suitable. Vegetative: leaves (bryophyllum), stem (turmeric), runners (grass), bulbs (onion), artificial cutting/grafting/layering/tissue culture.
sections.visual: 5 cards: fission planes, bud, Hydra fragmentation, sporangia, vegetative propagation by roots/stems

sections.title: Sexual — Mitosis vs Meiosis
sections.content: Mitosis: somatic, chromosome number maintained, 2 diploid daughters, for growth/repair. Meiosis: sex cells, half chromosomes, 4 haploid, for gamete formation.
sections.visual: Mitosis 2n→2n vs Meiosis 2n→n→n diagram

sections.title: Human Reproduction — Male & Female Systems
sections.content: Male: testes (seminiferous tubules → sperms, Leydig → testosterone) in scrotum, epididymis, vas deferens, urethra, prostate+seminal vesicles → semen, penis. Female: ovaries (ova, estrogen/progesterone), oviducts, uterus (fetal development), vagina. Menstruation: cyclic ovum release, endometrium sheds if no fertilization, 28 days via LH,FSH, estrogen, progesterone. Fertilization: sperm+egg→zygote→embryo→fetus.
sections.visual: Male/female system diagrams, 28-day cycle wheel

sections.title: Contraception & Health
sections.content: Barrier (condoms, diaphragms — also STD prevention), hormonal (pills, emergency), IUD (intrauterine, years), surgical (vasectomy, tubal ligation), unreliable (coitus interruptus, rhythm). Health = STD + unwanted pregnancy prevention.
sections.visual: Contraception matrix: barrier/hormonal/IUD/surgical with effectiveness

sections.title: Plants — Flower, Pollination, Fertilization
sections.content: Flower whorls: non-essential sepals/petals (protect, attract) and essential androecium (stamen: anther+filament → pollen) & gynoecium (pistil: stigma+style+ovary → ovule). Pollination: anther→stigma (self/cross via wind/water/insects/birds/bats). Fertilization: pollen→2 male nuclei on stigma, ovule has egg+2 polar nuclei → one male+polar→endosperm (3n), one+egg→zygote→embryo, ovary→fruit, ovule→seed.
sections.visual: Flower whorls, pollination agents, double fertilization (triploid endosperm + diploid zygote)

solvedExamples.q: Difference fission vs fusion?
solvedExamples.solution: Fission splits one into smaller (Paramecium), fusion fuses two smaller into larger (not reproduction here).

solvedExamples.q: What is fragmentation?
solvedExamples.solution: Parent breaks into fragments, each grows into new organism (Planaria).

sections.title: Environment & Ecosystem
sections.content: Surrounding where organism thrives: living (biotic: plants, animals, microbes) + non-living (abiotic: sunlight, air, water, soil, minerals). Ecosystem = biotic+abiotic interacting in area (pond, grassland). Nutrition: autotrophic (plants make own) vs heterotrophic (animals/fungi). Saprophytes/decomposers (fungi, bacteria, worms) break dead matter → nutrients for plants.
sections.visual: Pond ecosystem: biotic + abiotic circle

sections.title: Trophic Levels & Pyramids
sections.content: Trophic levels: T1 producers, T2 primary consumers (herbivores), T3 secondary, T4 tertiary/quaternary, decomposers. Pyramids: numbers, biomass, energy (always upright). Energy flow: 10% law — only 10% transferred to next level (1000J→100J→10J), rest lost as heat/incomplete eating.
sections.visual: Energy pyramid 1000→100→10, 10% arrows

sections.title: Food Chain & Web
sections.content: Food chain: series dependent as food (grass→deer→tiger). Food web: interconnections, who eats whom. Characteristics: summary of trophic levels, energy flow.
sections.visual: Chain vs web: linear vs net

sections.title: Pollution — Air, Ozone, Garbage
sections.content: Pollution: harmful materials via natural (volcano, fire) or human (carbon, runoff). Air: forest fire/dust/volcano vs power plants/industry. Ozone: CFCs deplete O3 → UV, need protection. Garbage: segregation→collection→transport→treatment→processing→disposal; biodegradable (plants/animals, decomposed by weather/microbes) vs non-biodegradable. Biodegradation via living processes.
